rows.description: A wise traveller asks several people for directions, checks answers against each other and keeps valuables close. Friendly help is common, but careful checking guards against wrong turns and opportunists.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child takes apart an old toy or torch to see inside, thrilled and unable to put it back. Tinkering builds understanding of mechanisms, and supervised access to safe tools makes it useful.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, curiosity, trust

rows.subtype: Fixing something with a family member [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager helps a parent or uncle fix a fan, cycle or tap and learns by watching hands and hearing why. Skills in many homes pass this way, and the sense of capability lasts a long time.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult uses an online video to fix a leaking pipe or a phone screen and is proud when it works and dismayed when it does not. Knowing which jobs are safe to attempt and which need a professional is part of the skill.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: An adult with a little experience fixes a wiring or gas problem without switching off the supply first. Small success breeds confidence, but some jobs are dangerous enough that a licensed person is the wise choice.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A householder unfamiliar with repairs feels helpless when a technician names a price and a problem they cannot verify. Asking for the fault to be shown, and sometimes for a second opinion, protects against both overcharging and needless work.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A capable person keeps basic tools in one place, uses the correct tool for each job and does small maintenance before things fail. Cheap prevention and proper tools avoid most costly repairs.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Pocket money and spending at once [Actor]
rows.description: A child given pocket money spends it on sweets the same day and later wants something bigger. Saving toward a goal is taught by feeling the difference between a wish now and a bigger wish later.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager with a first UPI app pays casually for snacks and games because tapping does not feel like spending. Digital payment removes the physical sense of money leaving, so tracking becomes a needed habit.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A wise teenager never shares a UPI PIN or OTP, does not approve a collect request they did not expect, and checks with a parent before paying a stranger. Scams rely on urgency, and pausing defeats them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
